title: What If People Left a Region for 40 Years? Chernobyl Shows It

scenes.text: What if humans abandoned a whole region for forty years? Chernobyl is the experiment.
After the April 1986 explosion, more than 100,000 people evacuated, and an exclusion zone of about 2,600 square kilometers was sealed off.
Camera traps there now photograph gray wolves, lynx, brown bears, and the wild Przewalski's horse.
A recent survey covered about 60,000 square kilometers of northern Ukraine, and nearly two thirds of 31,200 sightings came from the Chornobyl reserve.
Scientists point to one thing: almost no human activity in the zone, so large animals have the space.
The zone is still closed to normal life. But it shows how fast nature moves back in when we leave.
